title: Coherence Resonance Phenomena in an Atom-Dimer Two Mode BECs
abstract: We investigate the non-equilibrium dynamics of atomic-molecular Bose-Einstein condensates coupled via a Feshbach resonance, with Gaussian white noise acting on both the coupling strength and the detuning. Using the bosonic Josephson-junction and Bloch-sphere formalisms, we examine how coherence (coupling) noise and imbalance (detuning) noise modify the coherence-resonance point as functions of the initial polarization and the Feshbach detuning. Noise plays a more coherent role when its characteristic timescale matches the intrinsic timescales of the dynamics, leading to extrema in the time-averaged purity and the Husimi-Q distribution.
summary: This theoretical study examines how noise affects coherence resonance in BECs formed from coupled atoms and molecules via a Feshbach resonance. By using the Bloch-sphere formalism, the authors show that noise can induce resonant behavior, allowing researchers to map out optimal parameter regimes for controlling quantum coherence in these quantum gas systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates Coherence Resonance (CR) phenomena in the non-equilibrium dynamics of atomic-molecular Bose-Einstein Condensates (BECs) coupled via a Feshbach resonance.
main_result: The interplay between intrinsic system timescales and external noise sources can lead to noise-induced resonant behavior, which is characterized by extrema in coherence measures like purity and the Husimi-Q distribution.
method: The analysis employs the Bloch-sphere formalism and the large-N limit to derive and solve the stochastic evolution equations for the system's first moments.
model_or_system: The system is an atom-dimer two-mode BEC modeled as a two-level system, governed by a Hamiltonian including atom-atom, molecule-molecule, and atom-molecule interactions, coupled by a Feshbach resonance.
key_observables: Purity, Husimi-Q distribution, and the characteristic relaxation time scale ($T_i$).
important_parameters: Initial polarization, Feshbach detuning ($\epsilon_b$), and noise strengths ($\gamma_x, \gamma_z$).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses a single-mode condensate approximation and assumes the total particle number is conserved.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the real-time relaxation dynamics of the Bloch vector components under noise, and show the dependence of the characteristic time scale on initial polarization and detuning.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the Hamiltonian and dynamics using the Bloch-vector formalism, then analyzes the relaxation time scale by linearizing the equations, and finally examines how noise modifies the coherence resonance point by analyzing time-averaged coherence measures.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses noise-induced phenomena (Coherence Resonance) in a highly relevant platform (BECs), providing quantitative tools (Purity, Bloch formalism) to study non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.
